title: Cryptographically weak PRNG used to generate session identifiers
detail: `new_session_id()` generates session tokens using `random.choice()` from Python's `random` module (line 11). The `random` module uses a Mersenne Twister PRNG, which is not cryptographically secure and whose state can be reconstructed after observing a modest number of outputs. Session IDs must be unguessable; the standard remedy is `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` or equivalent.

title: SHA-1 used for password hashing — insufficient computational effort
detail: `password_hash()` hashes passwords with `hashlib.sha1((salt + password).encode()).hexdigest()` at line 15. SHA-1 is a general-purpose fast hash: on commodity hardware, billions of SHA-1 digests can be computed per second, making offline dictionary and brute-force attacks trivial. Password storage requires a slow, memory-hard function such as bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2.
